title: The Optimist Jazzers and the Gobert family
summary: Bill Craze brought him into the civic amateur-pro group, where he practiced his front line; C melody saxophones were popular.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: What about the Optimist Jazzers? That's a thing I forgot to ask about. That was a civic deal where the union let us play with the Optimist Club.

Bill Craze got me into that. Bill was a fine trombone player. And we had three amateurs and three pros. We had Bill Craze on the trombone, myself on the trumpet, Francis Murray, and I told you he was a fine tenor man. He played tenor and clarinet. Well that was really my front line. Every time we played with them we got some practice. I loaned Mr. Gobert's wife my chord book. And she studied piano. And she punched the chords. And Mr. Gobert, he played the Hoot Nanny. I played some washtub with a broomstick on it, and a bass fiddle string. He did a good job there. And poor John Connolly who passed away, he was a lawyer, he played the soprano sax and the C melody. That's way back. And another fine guy who passed away, T. Milton Hines, who had the finance company. He loved music. And he developed a beat after a while, and he would ride the drums for amateur things. Well I enjoyed playing with him.
The C melody was at all popular when you were coming up?

When I was coming up, most of the professors would sell you a C melody right off the back. Because you could play with the piano music. Go home and show Mama how quick you could play. I think that was more of a commercial deal. Raymond Baker played a C melody one night when I was with him, or in John. But the Alchemist Club was good practice for us, and we were treated royally by the Gobert family.
That's Lloyd and Betty, aren't they, the fireman department?
Lloyd, yeah. Ella, and I think he called his wife Betty. She used to be an airline hostess at one time before they were married. We had a lot of fun. And it was good rehearsing for my front line.
